origin.lesson: A return can erase a sampled departure from the final label. Changing the interior grid affects which departures are observed while leaving the endpoint observable unchanged.

operation.calculation: Take the start-to-away element of the sampled transition matrix raised to the number of base steps.
Coarsen the transition matrix to the observation stride. Raise its start-to-start element to the number of observed steps to find the probability of seeing no change.

limits: Conditional model forecasts for matching settings, a fixed decoder, known starting label, a homogeneous two-state transition matrix, and the declared sample grid. These forecasts do not identify the physical event rate between samples.
